sources.title: Noorul Hasan Ansari, Bahmanid Dynasty, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct specialist article read. Foundation 1347; Gulbarga then Bidar; last kings and 1528 endpoint. Other institutional chronology extends nominal dynasty to 1538, acknowledged publicly.

sources.title: Sharif Husain Qasemi, Bidar, Encyclopaedia Iranica
sources.note: Direct article read. Capital transfer in 1424, literary/performing arts, Gawan letters, college arrangement and tiles. Wrong elevation and unqualified claims of pervasive Persian influence excluded.

sources.title: Ghulam Yazdani, Bidar: Its History and Monuments (1947)
sources.note: Downloaded primary archaeological monograph and read local text. Printed pages 5, 7, 97 and 130; PDF pages 23, 25, 115 and 148. Historical schools and hospital claims rely on chroniclers cited by author; college cistern is a measured archaeological observation, underground supply explicitly apparent.

sources.title: Indira Gandhi National Open University, BHIC-107, Unit 5: Deccan Kingdoms
sources.note: Original indexed university chapter sections 5.12 and 5.13 read; direct PDF extraction failed. Nikitin observations kept as a traveler account rather than exhaustive class analysis or reliable head counts. Land measurement used without unsupported first-invention claim.

sources.title: Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO: Monuments and Forts of the Deccan Sultanate, tentative-list submission (2014)
sources.note: Direct submission read. This is India’s tentative-list submission, not an inscription as World Heritage. Used for covered Gulbarga mosque, Bidar moat controls and Ashtur tomb paintings. Bahmani and Barid modifications are not all attributed to one ruler.

sources.title: Navina Najat Haidar, Coins of the Bahmani and Vijayanagara Empires, in Sultans of Deccan India, 1500 to 1700 (Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2015)
sources.note: Downloaded museum catalogue; printed page 34 / human PDF page 51 visually checked in met-p34.png. Item 1i: Bidar, AH 876 / 1471 to 72, silver 11 g. Footnote 2 supplies exact Roman transliteration of Arabic inscription and English translation. Original Arabic glyphs not reconstructed. All derived prose charged against complete catalogue URL.

sources.title: Navina Haidar and Marika Sardar, Sultans of Deccan India: Exhibition Galleries (Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2015)
sources.note: Direct/indexed original exhibition text read. Describes Bahmani Empire as 1347 to 1538 and the five successor courts. Used to make conflicting nominal endpoints visible and distinguish political fragmentation from cultural disappearance.

proposedOverrides.name: Bahmani Kingdom
proposedOverrides.summary: A major Deccan sultanate whose late map window covers fragmentation into successor kingdoms.

batchIdentityNotes.indexWindow: 1500 to 1530, circa; alias Bahmani; only world-1500 snapshot
batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Founded 1347; Gulbarga first capital, Bidar capital from 1424. Imperial fragmentation predates and continues through imported window. Nominal dynastic endpoint differs between specialist sources, 1528 versus 1538; no manufactured single 1530 event.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded bbox 77.485, 16.017, 79.433, 16.311 is a very narrow east-west strip. It misses Gulbarga at about 17.34 N, 76.83 E and Bidar at about 17.92 N, 77.53 E, and cannot represent historic empire or even both capitals. Public overview states this major limitation.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: Earlier royal institutions are explicitly dated/contextualized. College cistern directly measured by archaeological monograph; schools/hospital derive from chronicles as summarized there. Tourist claims of tens of thousands of students, modern laboratories, original Bidri invention and confidently dated qanat construction not used. Writing is an attested scholarly transliteration, not inferred glyphs.
